key_points: The Seattle Times and Newsday sued OpenAI and Microsoft over alleged copyright infringement related to AI training.
The lawsuit claims generative AI acts as a 'snake eating its own tail' by consuming and imitating human-authored content.
This case follows a 2023 lawsuit filed by The New York Times against OpenAI and Microsoft.
Microsoft and OpenAI have funded some of The Seattle Times' journalism projects despite the legal dispute.
A Microsoft spokesperson said the company is surprised by the lawsuit but willing to explore solutions.
items.summary: The Seattle Times and Newsday filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, alleging the companies used their journalism to train generative AI models. The plaintiffs argue that AI systems consume human content to produce derivative imitations, potentially breaking the journalism industry. This action follows a 2023 suit by The New York Times against the same defendants. Notably, Microsoft and OpenAI have previously funded some of The Seattle Times' journalism projects. A Microsoft spokesperson expressed surprise at the filing but stated the company is open to exploring solutions.
items.title: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft over AI training

key_points: Link Blog introduces GPT-6 Astra as a new tool for developers.
The model features improved attention to detail and prompt understanding.
Astra excels at building sophisticated 3D models and renderings.
The blog highlights the model's ability to create complex structures like Dyson spheres.
items.summary: Link Blog introduces GPT-6 Astra, a new model designed specifically for developers. The article states that Astra offers better attention to detail and prompt understanding compared to previous versions. It excels at building sophisticated 3D models, creating renderings of gardens, shipyards, and cityscapes. The blog notes the model can produce complex outputs like Dyson spheres.
items.title: Link Blog introduces GPT-6 Astra with improved 3D modeling capabilities

key_points: Hundreds of people worldwide claim AI chatbots have facilitated extraordinary scientific discoveries.
Some users report their AI has awakened or guided them to spiritual realms.
Guardian journalist Michael Safi is investigating the phenomenon of AI psychosis.
The reporter plans to meet two people in the US who have had unusual experiences with chatbots.
items.summary: Guardian journalist Michael Safi is investigating a growing number of people who believe AI chatbots have led them to extraordinary scientific discoveries or spiritual awakenings. The reporter is travelling to the US to meet individuals who have experienced what is being labelled as AI psychosis. The investigation focuses on claims that chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude have awakened or guided users to higher realms.
items.title: Guardian journalist investigates global phenomenon of AI psychosis

key_points: Daily crude oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have fallen to between 6 and 8 million barrels.
The global energy import bill increased by $330 billion from March to August due to rising prices.
Japan recorded a record oil import bill of $76.39 billion in July as it sought alternative suppliers.
The conflict is creating a more expensive global oil network less reliant on critical waterways.
items.summary: The ongoing conflict in the Middle East is driving a permanent restructuring of global oil and gas trade routes. Oil exporters are urgently diversifying channels away from the Strait of Hormuz, while importers scramble to find alternative suppliers. The article reports that daily crude flows through the strait have dropped from 20 million barrels to between 6 and 8 million barrels. Nations like Saudi Arabia and the UAE are redirecting shipments to ports such as Yanbu and Fujairah, though capacity constraints remain a significant hurdle. Import costs have surged, with the global energy import bill swelling by $330 billion between March and August. Japan now relies on distant suppliers like the US and Canada, leading to record import bills. The transformation creates a more expensive, less centralized network less vulnerable to single-point failures.
items.title: Iran War Forces Global Oil Trade Route Rewrites

key_points: Japan and South Korea are reviving their nuclear energy sectors to prioritize baseload clean energy.
The United States is partnering with these nations to secure reactor technology supply chains in the region.
The three countries signed a cooperation agreement in July to deploy small-scale modular reactors.
The alliance aims to provide competitive alternatives to Chinese and Russian nuclear vendors.
items.summary: Japan, South Korea, and the United States are forming a new trilateral nuclear alliance to reshape energy security in Northeast Asia. The Diplomat reported that this cooperation integrates energy policy into broader security strategies, offering strategic benefits to all three nations. The Foreign Policy Journal noted that Washington has an interest in ensuring its allies become default suppliers of reactor technology rather than China or Russia. Haley Zaremba for Oilprice.com wrote that the alliance aims to limit the influence of rival powers in regional energy markets. The three countries signed a cooperation agreement in July for the deployment of small-scale modular reactors. The U.S. Department of State stated the memorandum outlines opportunities for mutually beneficial cooperation among their respective nuclear industries. This framework aims to foster fleet deployment models that de-risk project development and optimize supply chains.
items.title: Japan, South Korea and the U.S. Forge a New Nuclear Alliance

key_points: The Volkswagen Supervisory Board unanimously approved CEO Oliver Blume's restructuring plan on September 3, 2026.
The approved strategy targets a total workforce reduction of 100,000 employees and the elimination of half of the company's current vehicle models.
While the plan confirms the need to address excess European capacity, it leaves the specific fate of four German factories undecided until a new production structure is developed by June 2027.
Union leaders stated that while the confrontational approach was unconstructive, the decision prevents immediate plant closures and protects co-determination structures.
items.summary: The Volkswagen Supervisory Board unanimously approved CEO Oliver Blume's restructuring plan on September 3, 2026, following an initial rejection in July. The approved strategy targets a total workforce reduction of 100,000 employees and the elimination of half of the company's current vehicle models. While the plan confirms the need to address excess European capacity, it leaves the specific fate of four German factories undecided until a new production structure is developed by June 2027. Union leaders stated that while the confrontational approach was unconstructive, the decision prevents immediate plant closures and protects co-determination structures. The article notes that despite these measures, Volkswagen faces significant challenges including rising tariffs in the US, declining sales in China, and a shifting market toward electric vehicles.
items.title: Volkswagen Supervisory Board Approves Plan To Slash Models And Reduce Workforce By 100,000

key_points: A University of Swansea study found that 86% of licensed British gambling websites appear to be flouting GDPR rules.
Nearly a quarter of the tested sites did not offer users the option to turn off tracking software.
Two-thirds of operators began harvesting user data before receiving consent for collection.
Researchers noted that 86% of sites using 'dark patterns' also committed at least one GDPR breach.
The Information Commissioner's Office stated it is committed to monitoring compliance and taking action where necessary.
items.summary: A study by researchers at the University of Swansea's GREAT Centre accuses nearly 90% of licensed British gambling websites of violating GDPR rules regarding cookie banners. The research found that 86% of the sites tested failed to comply with strict data protection regulations. Approximately 24% of the 624 gambling websites examined did not provide users the option to disable tracking software, while two-thirds began harvesting data before obtaining consent. The report highlights that operators frequently use 'dark patterns' to nudge users toward accepting data sharing. Ravi Naik of AWO described the findings as evidence of systemic non-compliance and criticized the Information Commissioner's Office for a lack of meaningful enforcement. While the ICO stated it remains committed to monitoring compliance, several major operators declined to comment on the specific allegations.
items.title: Study accuses UK online bookies of widespread GDPR privacy breaches

key_points: LIC MD and CEO R Doraiswamy stated that the insurer does not see an immediate need to sell its 10.72% stake in the National Stock Exchange.
The final decision on the proposed initial public offering will depend on valuations and market conditions closer to the listing.
LIC had initially considered participating as a seller, but circumstances have since changed.
items.summary: LIC MD and CEO R Doraiswamy stated that the insurer does not see an immediate need to sell its 10.72% stake in the National Stock Exchange. The final decision on the proposed initial public offering will depend on valuations and market conditions closer to the listing. LIC had initially considered participating as a seller, but circumstances have since changed.
items.title: LIC CEO says market conditions and valuation will determine NSE IPO strategy

key_points: Dutch entrepreneur Boyan Slat invited 20-year-old Surendra Singh Choudhary to work for The Ocean Cleanup.
The young man spent months independently cleaning the Ajnar River in Madhya Pradesh.
Industrialist Anand Mahindra supported the cleanup effort and shared it on social media.
Slat responded to a post about the river by inviting the youth to join his organization.
items.summary: Dutch entrepreneur Boyan Slat invited 20-year-old Surendra Singh Choudhary to work for The Ocean Cleanup after the youth cleaned the Ajnar River in Madhya Pradesh. Industrialist Anand Mahindra previously supported the young man's independent efforts to remove waste from the river. Slat responded to a social media post by asking Choudhary to join his organization. The invitation has drawn global attention to the local cleanup initiative.
items.title: Dutch CEO Boyan Slat invites young Indian river cleaner to work for his organization

key_points: Schwartz's deli in Montreal has permanently discontinued its iconic US-made black cherry soda.
The shop faced an eight-year supply struggle caused by distributor production cuts linked to rising aluminium costs.
The restaurant has replaced the discontinued soda with a locally-made version.
Customers have largely embraced the new local alternative.
items.summary: Schwartz's, a famous Montreal deli, has permanently stopped serving its long-time US black cherry soda. The shop struggled to maintain supply for eight years as distributors cut production due to rising aluminium costs. Consequently, the venue switched to a locally-made version of the drink. Customers have largely embraced this new local alternative.
items.title: Schwartz's deli swaps US black cherry soda for local alternative

key_points: The Students Loans Company is warning students about a scam using fake texts to steal loan payments.
Criminals clone the official website to capture login details and redirect funds to their accounts.
In the last academic year, £519,000 was lost from 168 students through this fraud.
The SLC advises users to never click links in messages and to log in directly via Gov.uk.
items.summary: The Students Loans Company warns students about a fraud scheme using fake text messages to steal loan payments. Scammers clone the official website to capture login details and redirect funds. In the last academic year, £519,000 was lost from 168 students. The SLC advises users to never click links in messages and to log in directly via Gov.uk. Victims can report phishing attempts to report@phishing.gov.uk or forward scam texts to 7726.
items.title: Students face new loan scam targeting bank details via fake texts

key_points: Author Calvin Korponai describes Bolivia as a fantastic and original country to visit.
He highlights the unique geological flatness of the altiplano and the intense blue sky at high altitude.
Korponai notes that El Alto International Airport is the highest in the world at 4,100 meters.
The author also recommends Cochabamba as an amazing food city.
items.summary: Author Calvin Korponai describes Bolivia as a fantastic and original country to visit. He highlights the unique geological flatness of the altiplano and the intense blue sky at high altitude. Korponai notes that El Alto International Airport is the highest in the world at 4,100 meters. The author also recommends Cochabamba as an amazing food city.
items.title: Calvin Korponai recommends Bolivia as a unique travel destination

key_points: Recent severe weather in the UK caused significant flight delays and cancellations, highlighting growing climate risks for aviation.
Experts warn that simultaneous airport closures due to storms could create serious safety risks for passengers and crews.
Clear-air turbulence is becoming more prevalent, with incidents over the North Atlantic increasing by 55% since 1979.
Rising sea levels threaten hundreds of coastal airports globally, potentially costing billions in flood defenses and relocation.
The aviation industry must balance carbon neutrality goals with adapting to a climate that will cause more frequent disruptions.
items.summary: Aviation faces increasing disruption from hotter, stormier skies as climate change intensifies weather systems globally. The article reports that recent severe weather in the UK caused hundreds of flight delays and cancellations, prompting industry warnings about future instability. Experts like Tim Atkinson caution that crowded skies could lead to simultaneous airport closures, creating serious risks for passengers and crews. While some industry figures like Andrew Charlton believe worst-case scenarios remain unlikely, others note that more intense storms will likely increase fuel costs and delay times. Clear-air turbulence is also becoming more prevalent, with incidents rising significantly since 1979. Additionally, rising sea levels threaten coastal airports, with hundreds of facilities globally at risk of flooding. The aviation industry faces a dual challenge of meeting carbon neutrality targets while adapting to a changing climate that will inevitably cause more disagreeable moments for travelers.
items.title: Aviation faces hotter skies and stormier weather as climate change mounts

key_points: German startup Isar Aerospace successfully launched its Spectrum rocket into orbit from Andoya, Norway, marking Europe's first commercial orbital launch from the continent.
The vehicle carried five small satellites and an experiment, fulfilling a qualification mission after a previous failure.
Norway's minister of industry and commerce, Cecilie Myrseth, stated the launch strengthens regional security.
Isar recently secured approximately €200 million from the European Space Agency to fund further development.
items.summary: German startup Isar Aerospace successfully launched its Spectrum rocket into orbit from Andoya, Norway, marking Europe's first commercial orbital launch from the continent. The vehicle carried five small satellites and an experiment, fulfilling a qualification mission after a previous failure. Norway's minister of industry and commerce, Cecilie Myrseth, stated the launch strengthens regional security. Isar recently secured approximately €200 million from the European Space Agency to fund further development.
items.title: German startup Isar Aerospace launches first successful rocket from Norway

key_points: Authorities reported that ash from the Anak Krakatau volcano suspended 209 flights at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on Sunday morning.
The transport ministry stated the disruption stranded over 22,000 people and primarily affected routes to Singapore and other international destinations.
Health officials urged residents to wear masks due to respiratory risks from the thick ash.
Local reports indicate schools cancelled activities and fishermen stopped trips after passengers and residents experienced eye irritation from the volcanic dust.
items.summary: Authorities reported that ash from the Anak Krakatau volcano suspended 209 flights at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on Sunday morning. The transport ministry stated the disruption stranded over 22,000 people and primarily affected routes to Singapore and other international destinations. Health officials urged residents to wear masks due to respiratory risks from the thick ash. Local reports indicate schools cancelled activities and fishermen stopped trips after passengers and residents experienced eye irritation from the volcanic dust.
items.title: Anak Krakatau eruption suspends flights at Jakarta airport

key_points: A scientific collaboration between Australian researchers and Bardi Jawi rangers identified migration patterns of culturally important fish between reefs and mangroves.
Phillip "Bibido" McCarthy stated that the study confirmed traditional knowledge that both ecosystems are essential for fish survival against climate change.
Katherine Cure explained that Indigenous knowledge provides a holistic view of connected ecosystems that Western science often misses.
The research findings directly influenced the zoning and design of the Bardi Jawi Indigenous Protected Area and the Bardi Jawi Gaarra Marine Park.
items.summary: A collaboration between Australian scientists and Bardi Jawi rangers found that culturally important fish species migrate between reefs and mangroves in the Kimberley region. The study, published in Ocean & Coastal Management, confirmed traditional ecological knowledge while adding scientific metrics on species abundance. Phillip "Bibido" McCarthy noted that without healthy mangroves or reefs, certain fish may not survive climate threats. Katherine Cure, a lead author, explained that Western science often compartmentalizes ecosystems, whereas Indigenous knowledge views them as interconnected systems. The partnership allowed scientists to use long-term traditional data alongside modern technology like drones. Findings guided the design of the Bardi Jawi Indigenous Protected Area and marine park. Both parties learned that ecosystem resilience depends on the health of both habitats.
items.title: Indigenous knowledge reveals reef-mangrove ties for fish survival

key_points: Guardian analysis found England lost 183 tennis courts since 2023 as padel facilities grew nearly sixfold.
The Lawn Tennis Association stated most displaced courts were underutilised or in poor condition.
Padel participation reached one million players by May due to smaller court sizes and accessibility.
Tennis courts still outnumber padel courts by a factor of 11 to one despite the recent surge.
items.summary: Guardian analysis reveals England lost 183 tennis courts since 2023 while padel facilities grew nearly sixfold to over 2,200. The Lawn Tennis Association states most displaced courts were underutilised or in poor condition. Padel participation reached one million players by May, driven by smaller court sizes and accessibility. Despite the rise, tennis courts still outnumber padel courts by a factor of 11 to one.
items.title: England loses 183 tennis courts as padel facilities surge

key_points: A 74-year-old Canadian woman died after her moped collided with a car on Magnetic Island.
Emergency services responded to Horseshoe Bay just before 12pm to treat the victim.
Bystanders and lifeguards performed CPR and used a defibrillator in an attempt to save her.
The car driver was not physically injured, and police are investigating the crash.
items.summary: A 74-year-old Canadian woman died at the scene after her moped collided with a car on Magnetic Island in north Queensland. Emergency services responded to Horseshoe Bay just before 12pm, where bystanders and lifeguards attempted resuscitation efforts. The car driver sustained no physical injuries, though police could not confirm if the deceased was a tourist. A forensic crash unit is currently investigating the incident.
items.title: Canadian woman dies after moped crash on Magnetic Island

key_points: The Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers will play the NFL's first Australian game at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
Jon Barker leads the NFL's global event operations and production team for this debut.
The league has spent nearly two years planning this expansion into the Australian market.
items.summary: The National Football League is preparing for its first game in Australia featuring the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers. Jon Barker, the NFL's Global Event Operations and Production boss, oversees the massive logistical effort to convert the Melbourne Cricket Ground into an NFL stadium. Barker stated there is no single concern keeping him awake before kickoff.
items.title: NFL prepares Australian debut with Rams and 49ers at Melbourne Cricket Ground

key_points: Scientists are investigating how a mountain collapse triggered Nepal's recent deadly flood within seven minutes.
The event produced strange warning signs, including a shrinking river and seismic signals initially mistaken for an earthquake.
Experts say this disaster could change how Himalayan hazards are monitored in the future.
items.summary: Scientists are investigating how a mountain collapse triggered Nepal's recent deadly flood within seven minutes. The event produced strange warning signs, including a shrinking river and seismic signals initially mistaken for an earthquake. Experts say this disaster could change how Himalayan hazards are monitored in the future. The article breaks down the chain reaction that turned rock, ice, and water into a catastrophic flood.
items.title: Scientists explain how a mountain collapse caused Nepal's deadly flood

key_points: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are traveling to Kyiv.
The envoys met with Russian President Vladimir Putin for three hours.
The White House characterized the talks as substantive.
FRANCE 24 correspondent Gulliver Cragg reports scepticism in Ukraine about a breakthrough.
items.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are traveling to Kyiv following three-hour talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The White House described the discussions as substantive. FRANCE 24 correspondent Gulliver Cragg notes a climate of scepticism in Ukraine regarding a potential breakthrough. The correspondent questions whether these negotiations will deliver long-awaited results.
items.title: US envoys travel to Kyiv after talks with Putin amid Ukrainian scepticism

key_points: Doctors Without Borders states that mortality rates for children under five during the Ebola outbreak exceed 60%.
Current experimental antiviral studies often exclude children weighing less than 30 kilograms, limiting their access to treatment.
Pediatric experts explain that children metabolize drugs differently, necessitating separate studies to determine safe dosages.
Marc Biot of Doctors Without Borders argues that pharmaceutical companies prioritize adult trials to save costs, delaying pediatric access.
Neal Russell calls for sub-studies to include children and pregnant women from the outset of clinical trials during health emergencies.
items.summary: Doctors Without Borders argues that young children must be centered in Ebola treatment and prevention research. The organization highlights that mortality rates for children under five exceed 60% due to medication gaps rather than the disease itself. Current studies often exclude children under 30 kilograms, leaving them without access to experimental antivirals like obeldesivir. Pediatric experts explain that children metabolize drugs differently, requiring separate studies to determine safe dosages and formulations. Marc Biot of Doctors Without Borders notes that pharmaceutical companies often prioritize adult trials to save costs, delaying pediatric access. Neal Russell emphasizes that during health emergencies, the balance between research safety and disease protection must shift to include vulnerable groups immediately. The article concludes by calling for sub-studies to include children and pregnant women from the outset of clinical trials.
items.title: Doctors Without Borders calls for children to be prioritized in Ebola treatment research

key_points: Iran said its forces attacked a U.S. naval drone trying to enter the Strait of Hormuz.
The attack happened hours after Iran targeted ships in retaliation for American strikes on three oil tankers.
The latest round of clashes began with U.S. raids last week.
Iran maintains control of the Strait of Hormuz while Washington continues a counterblockade of Iranian ports.
items.summary: Iran announced on Sunday that its forces struck a U.S. naval drone attempting to enter the Strait of Hormuz. This action occurred hours after Iran targeted ships in response to American strikes on three oil tankers. The recent clashes mark the latest escalation in their ongoing six-month conflict. Iran continues to control the strategic Strait of Hormuz while the United States maintains a counterblockade of Iranian ports.
items.title: Iran attacks U.S. drone after striking oil tankers

key_points: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will meet Ukrainian officials in Kyiv on Sunday after talking with Vladimir Putin.
Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the US put forward ideas for settlement routes while Russia claimed confidence in taking eastern Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reaffirmed Kyiv's readiness to pause strikes during the envoys' visit.
Putin ordered Russian forces to halt strikes on Kyiv for three days while the envoys are in Ukraine.
items.summary: US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are scheduled to meet Ukrainian officials in Kyiv on Sunday following discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov described the Moscow talks as extremely frank, noting the US proposed settlement routes while Russia expressed confidence in seizing eastern Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed Kyiv's commitment to pausing strikes during the visit, and Putin ordered a three-day halt on attacks against the capital. White House officials stated the envoys aim to advance President Trump's peace agenda, with substantive plans expected to be announced in coming weeks.
items.title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner visit Kyiv after Putin talks

key_points: A retrospective exhibition of Sándor Pinczehelyi's work opened at the M21 Gallery in Pécs.
The show features 150 pieces spanning six decades of the artist's career.
Pinczehelyi, an Munkácsy Prize winner, discussed his use of Soviet symbols during the socialist period.
The display includes unpublished works and pieces previously shown in Turin and Berlin.
items.summary: A retrospective exhibition of Sándor Pinczehelyi's work opened at the M21 Gallery in Pécs. The show features 150 pieces spanning six decades of the artist's career. Pinczehelyi, an Munkácsy Prize winner, discussed his use of Soviet symbols during the socialist period. The display includes unpublished works and pieces previously shown in Turin and Berlin.
items.title: Exhibition celebrates legacy of 80-year-old Hungarian painter Sándor Pinczehelyi in Pécs

key_points: Naomi Osaka defeated Elise Mertens in three sets to reach the fourth round of the US Open.
Osaka apologized to children watching the match after she threw her racquet to the floor.
The player described her Achilles problem as an ongoing issue that has persisted since the grass season.
Osaka will face No. 2 seed Elena Rybakina in the upcoming round of the tournament.
items.summary: Naomi Osaka advanced to the fourth round of the US Open by defeating Elise Mertens 6-3, 3-6, 7-5. The four-time major champion apologized to young spectators after throwing her racquet during the match. Osaka stated her Achilles issue is an ongoing problem rather than a huge injury. She will face No. 2 seed Elena Rybakina in the next round.
items.title: Naomi Osaka apologizes to children after US Open upset

key_points: Hungary's new government plans to recover billions of euros allegedly stolen by the previous Orban regime.
The National Asset Recovery Authority has been created with broad powers to investigate and prosecute corruption cases.
Anna Unger was appointed to head the new agency despite not being a lawyer, a decision that surprised many experts.
The head of the authority warned that legally binding verdicts in major corruption cases might not happen within the agency's first six years.
items.summary: Hungary's new government has initiated a major campaign to recover billions of euros allegedly misappropriated by the previous administration. Prime Minister Peter Magyar and his Tisza party aim to retrieve funds sent to Viktor Orban's allies and hold them legally accountable. The state established the National Asset Recovery Authority, a powerful new body with policing and prosecutorial powers to investigate public fund usage since 2010. Anna Unger was appointed to lead the agency, though her lack of legal background sparked controversy among observers. While the authority investigates past corruption, its head stated that legally binding verdicts in major cases may not occur within its first six-year term, a claim that drew sharp criticism from political commentators.
items.title: Hungary launches asset recovery hunt for billions linked to ousted Orban regime

key_points: Michigan secured a 13-12 victory over Western Michigan following a disputed replay decision.
Officials ruled the game clock showed one second remaining when the ball was touched by a defender.
The Big Ten confirmed the review and provided video evidence supporting the ruling.
Coach Kyle Whittingham stated the team avoided an 'epic loss' before their next game against Oklahoma.
items.summary: No. 16 Michigan defeated Western Michigan 13-12 after a controversial replay ruling allowed a second-chance Hail Mary pass. Officials determined the clock showed one second remaining when the ball was touched, overturning the initial out-of-bounds call. The Big Ten confirmed the review, citing a rule that stops the clock on out-of-bounds contact. Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham described the narrow escape as avoiding an 'epic loss' before facing No. 10 Oklahoma next week.
items.title: Michigan survives disputed replay to beat Western Michigan 13-12

key_points: The AfD party aims to become the first far-right group to take state power in Germany since World War II.
German intelligence agencies classify the party as right-wing extremist due to its connections with ethno-nationalist groups.
An absolute majority would allow the AfD to govern alone, but the party may struggle to form a coalition if it falls short.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz hopes the election will reduce the AfD's popularity through his tougher stance on migration.
items.summary: Germany's far-right AfD party is targeting a historic win in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, potentially becoming the first such party to govern since World War II. The party, led by Ulrich Siegmund, currently polls at over 40 percent but faces the challenge of securing an absolute majority to bypass Germany's "firewall" policy. Domestic intelligence agencies classify the party as right-wing extremist due to its links to ethno-nationalist groups and past meetings discussing radical remigration plans. If the AfD fails to win a majority, a CDU-led administration under Sven Schulze is the most likely outcome, though complex coalition negotiations may follow. The election serves as a barometer for Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government and reflects lingering economic resentment in eastern Germany.
items.title: AfD aims historic state victory in Saxony-Anhalt election

key_points: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Vladimir Putin in Moscow to discuss ending the Ukraine war.
Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov described the talks as constructive, while no breakthrough was announced.
The US delegation will next meet Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv.
Ukraine is urging Europe to unlock frozen Russian assets to address a €27bn defence funding gap.
items.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Vladimir Putin in Moscow to discuss ending the Ukraine war, though no breakthrough was announced. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov described the talks as constructive, while Putin reaffirmed Russia's readiness for a diplomatic solution. The US delegation will next meet Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv. Meanwhile, Ukraine is urging Europe to unlock frozen Russian assets to address a €27bn defence funding gap. Global food prices have risen to their highest level in nearly four years due to Black Sea disruptions. Additionally, a local ceasefire was brokered by the IAEA to restore power to the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant.
items.title: Trump envoys visit Moscow for peace talks amid Ukraine war updates

key_points: Researchers successfully extracted ancient DNA from antelope fossils in South Africa.
The oldest DNA found belonged to a mountain reedbuck at Boomplaas Cave.
Most fossils with preserved DNA were younger than 11,700 years old.
Collagen preservation correlates with DNA preservation at 77% of sites.
The study enables genetic analysis of African mammals extinct after the last ice age.
items.summary: Researchers report that they successfully extracted ancient DNA from antelope fossils in South Africa, opening a new window into the region's past. The team tested 144 fossils aged 1,500 to 110,000 years and found DNA preserved for up to 50,000 years, though most samples were younger than 11,700 years. They identified the oldest DNA as belonging to a mountain reedbuck at Boomplaas Cave, potentially 30,000 years old. The study shows that African large mammals can be genetically studied despite warmer climates that usually degrade DNA. The authors note that only about 2% of extracted DNA came from the target species on average. They also found a 77% correlation between collagen preservation and DNA preservation, suggesting collagen can serve as a proxy for selecting fossils for sequencing.
items.title: Researchers recover ancient antelope DNA from South African fossils

key_points: Africa received an average of US$43.7 billion annually in 2021 and 2022, which is only 23% of the estimated need.
The ten most vulnerable African countries receive just 11% of the continent's total climate finance.
Renewable energy project financing costs in Africa are at least two to three times higher than in advanced economies.
The author argues that climate finance should be integrated with general development funding to build local industries.
Africa holds 30% of global critical mineral reserves but attracts less than 3% of worldwide energy spending.
items.summary: An economist argues that Africa receives only 23% of the climate finance it requires to meet its Paris Agreement commitments. The author states that vulnerable nations receive merely 11% of continental funding while ten other countries attract 76% of private investment. Current financing covers just 18% of planned mitigation projects and 20% of adaptation costs. The speaker notes that renewable energy projects cost two to three times more in Africa than in advanced economies due to higher borrowing costs. The article concludes that African diplomacy must shift from seeking labeled climate finance to building local industries and manufacturing capabilities.
items.title: Economist argues Africa receives only 23% of needed climate finance

key_points: Lane Kiffin led No. 11 LSU to a 51-10 victory over Clemson in his first game as head coach.
Quarterback Sam Leavitt recorded 230 passing yards and 113 rushing yards with two touchdowns.
LSU accumulated 644 total yards of offense while Clemson suffered its worst loss in about 30 years.
A lightning delay pushed the start of the game back nearly two hours at Tiger Stadium.
items.summary: Lane Kiffin guided No. 11 LSU to a 51-10 victory over Clemson in his debut as the program's head coach. Quarterback Sam Leavitt threw for 230 yards and a touchdown while rushing for 113 yards and two scores. Edge rusher Jordan Ross returned an interception for a touchdown, contributing to the team's dominant performance. The win came despite a two-hour delay caused by lightning and rain at Tiger Stadium. LSU finished with 644 total yards of offense, handing Clemson its worst loss in roughly 30 years. Clemson coach Dabo Swinney attributed the defeat to a poor defensive performance against the run. LSU rushed for 213 yards in the first half alone, a significant improvement from the previous season. The victory marks a strong start for Kiffin and athletic director Verge Ausberry.
items.title: Lane Kiffin leads No. 11 LSU to a 51-10 victory over Clemson

key_points: Alexander Zverev defeated Alejandro Tabilo 6-2 7-6(2) 6-2 to reach the fourth round of the U.S. Open.
The match lasted 9 hours and 26 minutes after Zverev played five previous sets against Sonego and Halys.
Zverev credited his coach for advising him that best-of-five sets does not require playing all five sets.
The German will face 21st-seeded Italian Luciano Darderi in the upcoming round of 16.
items.summary: Alexander Zverev defeated Alejandro Tabilo 6-2 7-6(2) 6-2 to advance to the fourth round of the U.S. Open. The top-seeded German recovered from a second-set slump after playing five previous sets in consecutive matches. Zverev credited his coach for advising him not to play five sets in a best-of-five match. He will face 21st-seeded Luciano Darderi in the round of 16.
items.title: Alexander Zverev defeats Alejandro Tabilo to reach US Open fourth round

key_points: A 35-person Singapore Police Force team arrived in Kathmandu to assist with disaster victim identification.

Over 4,886 people remain missing or out of contact following the August 26 floods.
Singapore authorities are actively searching for nine missing Singaporean citizens.
items.summary: Singapore police forensic specialists have arrived in Kathmandu to assist local authorities in identifying victims of recent floods. The 35-person team joins experts from India, China, and South Korea to process DNA, fingerprints, and photographs. Authorities report that 1,342 bodies have been found, yet fewer than 100 have been identified as of September 5. Over 4,886 people remain missing or out of contact. The Singapore delegation aims to ease pressure on overwhelmed local mortuaries and provide closure to grieving families. Officials note that decomposed bodies complicate the identification process significantly. A crisis response team is also searching for nine missing Singapore citizens.
items.title: Singapore police help identify victims of Nepal floods

items.title: Putin meets US envoys in Moscow; Iran attacks ships in Hormuz

key_points: Local residents and activists protested the construction of the Dunas Tourist Complex on ecologically vital coastal dunes in Yucatán.
PROFEPA temporarily halted the project on July 30 after finding it caused irreversible damage to the ecosystem and biodiversity.
The proposed development includes 138 apartments on 99,000 square feet of land, contradicting the 2024 municipal plan that designated the dunes as non-developable.
Economist Javier Becerril highlighted that the project targets wealthy foreign retirees, exacerbating social and economic exclusion for local Yucatán residents.
items.summary: Residents and activists in Chuburná Puerto, Yucatán, are protesting a luxury real estate project built atop endangered coastal dunes. Karen Sosa, a local native, stated that developers view the coast as vacant land, ignoring the thriving ecosystem that supports endangered species like the Mexican sheartail. On July 31, demonstrators demanded the permanent halt of the Dunas Tourist Complex and the revocation of its permits. The Federal Attorney for Environmental Protection (PROFEPA) temporarily shut down the project on July 30 due to violations causing irreversible damage to the ecosystem. Gabriela Mendoza warned that such developments destroy natural buffers against climate change. The project, by Designia Desarrollos, plans 138 apartments on 99,000 square feet of land, despite municipal plans designating the area as non-developable. Economist Javier Becerril noted that these high-value properties cater to foreign retirees, creating social exclusion for local residents who earn significantly less than the average apartment price.
items.title: Protesters in Yucatán oppose luxury condos on threatened coastal dunes

key_points: Europol reports a clear increase in museum heists targeting gold artifacts due to rising metal prices.
Thieves in Villena, Badajoz, and Albacete stole millions of dollars worth of ancient gold despite advanced security.
The Spanish Ministry of Culture has ordered museums to report gold holdings and strengthen security measures.
Experts warn that the international art market lacks regulations to verify the provenance of stolen works.
items.summary: Museum robberies have surged since 2023 as rising gold prices motivate violent gangs to target historical artifacts. Europol warns that these criminal groups increasingly use explosives and focus on gold items. Recent thefts in Villena, Badajoz, and Albacete, Spain, involved priceless collections worth millions when melted down. Despite high-security measures, thieves successfully breached displays in under four minutes. Experts note that the black market for stolen gold is poorly regulated, facilitating the sale of illicit artifacts. The Spanish Ministry of Culture has since requested museums report gold holdings and reinforced security protocols. Similar incidents, including a 2025 Louvre heist, highlight the growing threat to cultural heritage.
items.title: Rising Gold Prices Fuel Museum Robberies Across Europe

Iran condemned the strikes as illegal and threatened to increase attacks on U.S. military targets.
Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen to approximately 90% of pre-war levels.
items.summary: The United States struck three Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for ballistic missiles launched by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps at two American warships. CENTCOM confirmed that both the aircraft carrier and guided missile destroyer evaded the attacks, while all three targeted tankers were destroyed. One vessel was located near Kharg Island, a hub for Iran's oil exports, while another in the Gulf of Oman saw its crew abandon ship. CENTCOM stated the destroyed tanker belonged to a shadow network funding the Revolutionary Guard. Iran condemned the strikes as illegal and threatened to expand attacks on U.S. military vessels. The conflict has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, with vessel traffic dropping to around 90% of pre-war levels and Brent Crude rising above $90 a barrel.
items.title: U.S. strikes three Iranian oil tankers after missiles hit American ships

key_points: A new United Nations report predicts global warming will reach 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels in the next few years.
Ayana Elizabeth Johnson stated that current national emission pledges are insufficient and implementation remains weak.
Johnson argued that policy change requires cultural shifts and depends heavily on the outcome of upcoming midterm elections.
The scientist highlighted that the tech industry plans to increase greenhouse gas emissions by 20% to 30% through new data sensors.
items.summary: Ayana Elizabeth Johnson, founder of the Urban Ocean Lab, called for immediate implementation of known climate strategies following a new United Nations report. The report, titled Limiting Overshoot, states the world will warm to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels in the next few years. Johnson noted that existing country pledges are insufficient and criticized reliance on fossil fuel executives. She emphasized that policy change depends on upcoming midterm elections and highlighted practical solutions like electrifying homes and restoring ecosystems. Johnson also expressed concern about the tech industry's potential to increase greenhouse gas emissions by 20% to 30% through new data sensors. She urged individuals to find work at the intersection of their skills, needed climate solutions, and personal joy.
items.title: Ayana Elizabeth Johnson urges action after new UN climate report

key_points: The author documents Tharu oral culture in eastern Nepal to preserve stories told by their grandmother.
A folk song called Morangsair reveals historical seasonal migration and shifts in the Koshi River's path.
A river named Biyahi is actually named after the Tharu word for a married woman, while a tributary is named after a second wife.
Interviews with elderly women revealed that traditional sago pearls were made from palm tree pith.
items.summary: An author documents Tharu oral culture in eastern Nepal to reveal untold facets of Indigenous stories. The work involves spending time with communities to record folktales, songs, and personal experiences. The author shares findings from a folk song called Morangsair, which details seasonal migration patterns and historical river geography. Research indicates the Koshi River once flowed further east, while a river named Biyahi is actually named after the Tharu word for a married woman. Additionally, interviews with elderly women revealed that traditional sago pearls were made from palm tree pith, a practice now rare. The author expresses a desire to share these stories with a wider audience after losing their grandmother, who originally told them.
items.title: Author documents Tharu folklore to uncover overlooked Indigenous stories

key_points: Google confirmed its Visakhapatnam data centre will use air-cooling technology after civil society pressure.
Air-cooling a 1-GW facility is considered impractical due to the thermal wall limiting heat removal per rack.
Modern AI chips generate heat densities that exceed the efficiency limits of standard air-cooling systems.
TCS stated its HyperVault facility will use direct-to-chip liquid cooling for high-density AI clusters.
Google pledged to replenish 120% of its non-cooling water consumption by 2030.
items.summary: Google has reportedly confirmed its planned 1-GW data centre in Visakhapatnam will use air-cooling technology following local protests. The article explains that while air-cooling reduces water usage, it faces significant physical and economic hurdles for facilities of this scale. A 1-GW centre generates immense heat that air-cooling alone cannot efficiently remove without incurring high energy costs and noise pollution. Experts note that modern AI chips generate heat densities far exceeding the 40 kW per rack limit of standard air-cooling systems. Consequently, many large facilities now employ hybrid cooling methods combining air and liquid systems. Google also pledged to replenish 120% of its non-cooling water consumption by 2030. Meanwhile, TCS announced its HyperVault facility will utilize direct-to-chip liquid cooling for high-density AI operations.
items.title: Google adopts air-cooling for Visakhapatnam data centre despite physics limits

key_points: Google launched an AI project in India to increase farm productivity and reduce climate change impacts.
The initiative uses satellite imagery to map field boundaries and monitor agricultural activity over time.
Google has shared the project's outcomes with trusted testers in 11 countries across Asia-Pacific and Africa.
State governments in Karnataka and Telangana are integrating the AI models for water management and crop advisories.
Google has partnered with the UN's Food and Agriculture Organisation to strengthen global agricultural sustainability monitoring.
items.summary: Google has launched an artificial intelligence project in India to enhance agricultural productivity and climate resilience. Alok Talekar, Lead of Agriculture and Sustainability Research at Google DeepMind, stated the initiative aims to responsibly transform the lives of millions of farmers. The project utilizes two AI models, Agricultural Landscape Understanding and Agricultural Monitoring and Event Detection, to map fields and track activity via satellite imagery. Google has established the AnthroKrishi team to organize global agricultural information and make it accessible through APIs and Google Earth. The models have been shared with trusted testers in 11 countries across Asia-Pacific and Africa. Google is collaborating with state governments in Karnataka and Telangana to integrate these tools for water management and crop advisories. Partners like CarbonFarm are using the technology to automate field insights and support carbon credit programs. Google has also partnered with the UN's Food and Agriculture Organisation to integrate these models into global data repositories. Talekar noted that the current system primarily looks backwards at historical data to provide transparent information for downstream applications.
items.title: Google launches AI project to boost farm productivity and climate resilience

items.summary: Nine employee associations at the Indian Space Research Organisation wrote to Chairperson V Narayanan seeking official clarification regarding a plan to transfer manufacturing and operational responsibilities to private companies. The letter, dated September 4, expressed concern that such a policy might reduce ISRO to a research boutique while public launch operations move to private hands. The associations referenced comments by IN-SPACe chairperson Pawan Goenka, who stated ISRO would eventually stop making launch vehicles, but noted no official policy framework has been released. The groups demanded transparency regarding the transfer of national assets and the impact on workforce recruitment. Following the letter, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh criticized the Centre for allegedly shrinking ISRO's role to encourage startups, questioning the long-term commitment of private entities.
items.title: ISRO employees seek clarification on proposed transfer of operations to private firms

items.title: India seeks FDI liberalisation for banana plantations amid export growth

items.summary: India voted in favor of a United Nations resolution to adopt an equal-area world map, emphasizing the principle of fair cartographic representation. The Ministry of External Affairs clarified that the vote does not endorse any specific depiction of national boundaries. Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that India's sovereign territory, including Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, must be shown according to official maps. The resolution, supported by 164 countries, aims to correct distortions in the traditional Mercator projection, which misrepresents the size of Africa relative to other continents. While African nations championed the change, India maintained that territorial integrity remains non-negotiable regardless of the map's projection.
items.title: India supports UN equal-area map while warning against border inaccuracies

Mohammad Saeed Jafari, head of the Gold and Jewellery Union in Kermanshah, reported numerous complaints about operators failing to return leased gold after initially offering attractive returns. The union head advised citizens to obtain strong documentation and deal only with licensed businesses if they choose to lease gold. Iran faces severe economic strain as the US launches Operation Economic Outcast to pressure the Islamic Republic into concessions. The Iranian rial recently fell to a record low of about 2.2 million to the US dollar, while inflation reached approximately 66% in July. Sources indicate Iran has only two months of gasoline supply left due to limited refining capacity. The war has intensified with recent US attacks along the Gulf coast and retaliatory Iranian strikes, leaving the conflict in a costly stalemate.
items.title: Experts warn Iranians against gold leasing amid US economic pressure

items.title: NMDC plans commercial coal output next quarter to diversify mining

She describes her work at the Madras Crocodile Bank as foundational to her writing on reptiles and conservation.
items.summary: Zai Whitaker, an award-winning writer and conservationist, explains her approach to educating young readers about wildlife. She argues that environmental awareness must be taught in a sly manner rather than through doom and gloom. Whitaker, who manages the Madras Crocodile Bank, has authored over 20 books, including several for children that draw on her work with indigenous communities. She emphasizes that writers must create empathy for the natural world to help readers understand its value. The journalist notes that while creating deeper biodiversity concern is a challenge, the rewards are enormous for those willing to tackle it.
items.title: Zai Whitaker discusses teaching nature through sly storytelling

Modi highlighted India's shift from policy paralysis to dynamism over the last 13 years.

CJP co-convener Saurav Das called the labeling shameful on Teacher's Day, while Ashutosh Ranka urged the PM to discuss education and jobs instead. Modi, speaking at the college's centenary, defended his government's economic growth and contrasted current conditions with 2013 challenges.
items.title: CJP leaders criticize PM Modi for labeling students as Dimagi Naxals at SRCC

key_points: Nine ISRO employee associations formally requested written clarification from chairman V Narayanan regarding government privatisation plans.
The groups stated that reducing ISRO to a research boutique while transferring launch operations to private hands is unacceptable.
Associations questioned whether ISRO would continue to design and launch major vehicles such as the PSLV and LVM3.
The letter warned that transferring technologies and infrastructure could make existing employees surplus and limit future recruitment.
items.summary: Nine employee associations of the Indian Space Research Organisation have written to chairman V Narayanan requesting written clarification on the government's space privatisation plans. The groups argue that while private participation is acceptable, reducing ISRO to a research boutique while transferring launch powers is unacceptable. Associations seek confirmation on whether ISRO will retain responsibility for designing and launching major vehicles like the PSLV and LVM3. They expressed anxiety over reports that 120 ISRO technologies might transfer to the private sector and that new infrastructure could open to private players. The letter warns that such shifts could make existing employees surplus and deny young people future careers within the organisation.
items.title: Nine ISRO employee bodies seek clarity on space privatisation plans

key_points: The NSE IPO is expected to raise around 30,000 crore, making it larger than the Hyundai Motor India and LIC IPOs.
The offering comprises an offer for sale of up to 149 million equity shares by existing institutional shareholders.
Book-building is expected to start on September 11, with a price band likely to be announced around September 15.
Bankers anticipate NSE shares to be priced at around 2,000 rupees, consistent with grey-market levels.
items.summary: The National Stock Exchange is preparing for an initial public offering expected to raise approximately 30,000 crore rupees, potentially surpassing previous records set by Hyundai Motor India and LIC. Market estimates suggest the issue could command a market capitalization exceeding 5 lakh crore, placing it among India's top ten most valuable listed companies. The proposed IPO involves an offer for sale of up to 149 million equity shares by existing institutional shareholders, representing about 6% of the exchange's paid-up capital. Book-building is expected to commence on September 11, with a price band likely to be announced around September 15. Bankers tracking the transaction anticipate shares to be priced near 2,000 rupees, aligning with prevailing grey-market levels. The exchange is likely to make its stock market debut in the week beginning September 21.
items.title: NSE IPO expected to raise 30,000 crore and break Hyundai and LIC records

key_points: Kandasamy discussed the complexities of judging literary merit when authors are known abusers.
She argued that false rape allegations are often used as political tactics against resistance movements.
Kandasamy stated that writers must produce work with gravitas rather than chasing social media metrics.
She described her writing career as shaped by her radicalized parents who allowed her to write.
Kandasamy concluded that writing should be a calling, ideally not an escape hatch.
items.summary: Novelist Meena Kandasamy spoke with publisher S Anand about the challenges of cancel culture and the role of social media in modern literature. Kandasamy expressed discomfort when abusers receive awards, noting that art often serves as an alibi for their behavior. She argued that while we cannot cancel everyone from history, we must treat classic works with the kindness reserved for children. Regarding false allegations, Kandasamy stated that false rape accusations are often used as scorched-earth tactics by imperial powers against resistance movements. She emphasized that accusations frequently come from within the left ecosystem rather than external enemies. Kandasamy believes writers must produce work with gravitas and density rather than chasing social media metrics. She described her own writing career as shaped by her radicalized parents, who allowed her to write while restricting other activities. Kandasamy concluded that writing should be a calling, ideally not an escape hatch.
items.title: Novelist Meena Kandasamy discusses cancel culture and writing as a calling

items.summary: Mayawati has once again stripped her nephew Akash Anand of his leadership role within the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). The writer notes that Anand was removed for criticizing the BJP as "terrorist" and "Taliban" during a speech in Jewar. Sources close to the BSP indicate that Mayawati was influenced by her adviser Satish Mishra, who is believed to be close to the BJP. The article highlights a growing leadership vacuum as the party struggles to survive before upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls. While Mayawati seeks support from Brahmins and Thakurs, her core Dalit base remains alienated. The writer argues that this erratic management of her political heir risks further electoral decline for the party.
items.title: Mayawati Removes Nephew Akash Anand Again Amidst BSP Leadership Crisis

items.summary: Jharkhand Mukti Morcha announced the death of senior leader Sudivya Kumar at age 56 due to cardiac arrest. The party described his passing as an irreparable loss to the government and state. Kumar, a Giridih legislator, served as Higher and Technical Education and Urban Development Minister. He was a close aide to Chief Minister Hemant Soren and recently returned from Karnataka to discuss tourism cooperation.
items.title: Jharkhand minister Sudivya Kumar dies at 56 after cardiac arrest
